Poss-SLPC sro Unveils New High-Strength Steel Product in Slovakia

Žilina, Slovakia — Steel manufacturer Poss-SLPC sro has announced the launch of its newest high-strength steel product, marking what company officials describe as a significant step in supporting Slovakia’s industrial and construction sectors. The product, named FerraX 700, was showcased at a launch event held at the company’s main facility near Žilina on Monday, drawing representatives from regional industry groups, government officials, and business partners.

According to Poss-SLPC sro, FerraX 700 is engineered for enhanced durability and flexibility, targeting applications in infrastructure projects, heavy machinery, and transportation equipment. “This launch demonstrates our ongoing commitment to innovation and meeting the demands of Slovakia’s growing industries,” said Tomáš Baláž, Chief Executive of Poss-SLPC sro. “We have invested significantly in research and development over the past two years to bring FerraX 700 to market, and we are confident it will set new benchmarks in performance and reliability.”

The company revealed that the new steel grade features an optimized alloy composition and advanced rolling techniques developed in collaboration with the Slovak Technical Institute. Initial production capacity is expected to reach 40,000 tonnes annually, with plans to scale up based on market demand. Poss-SLPC sro currently employs over 600 workers at its Žilina facility, and company officials noted that the launch is expected to create 30 additional jobs in production and quality control.

Industry analysts say the introduction of FerraX 700 could bolster Slovakia’s reputation as a hub for advanced materials manufacturing. “With infrastructure investment on the rise across Central Europe, demand for high-strength, durable steels is increasing,” commented Martina Kováčová, a metals sector analyst at Danube Market Insights. “Poss-SLPC sro’s focus on innovation positions them well to serve both domestic and regional clients.”

Local officials also welcomed the development. “The launch of new products like FerraX 700 supports our regional economy and provides opportunities for skilled workers,” said Ján Hrivnák, Deputy Mayor of Žilina, at the event. He added that collaborations between the private sector and research institutions are vital to maintaining Slovakia’s competitiveness in the steel industry.

The first shipments of FerraX 700 are scheduled for July, with orders reportedly secured from construction firms and equipment manufacturers in Slovakia and neighboring countries. Poss-SLPC sro indicated that further product innovations are currently in development, with announcements expected later this year.
